content:
We have search results list of templates. Need to find the template that when applied to the molecule (product) reproduces the electrophilic bromination of aromatic ring. The product given in input is Nc1c(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c1Cl (an aniline with multiple chlorines). Wait bromination would add Br to aromatic ring, but product shows many Cl, not Br. However the task: "The Electrophilic Bromination of an aromatic ring involves substitution of a hydrogen atom on the aromatic ring with a bromine atom... halide functional group is formed." The retrosynthetic step: we need to break C-Br bond to get precursor with H. Our target molecule is the product after bromination? Actually the product should have Br, but the given SMILES has only Cl and N. Maybe the template search is for halogenation (Cl) but they want bromination. However we need to find template that matches the forward reaction (bromination). The search gave many templates with Cl. We need a template that introduces Br. Let's search again with functional_groups_formed: halide, but maybe need to specify bond formed C-Br. The tool expects bonds_formed format like "6-6". Not helpful. Could search without bond criteria, just halide formed. Already got many templates, but they involve Cl. Need one with Br. Let's search again with product containing Br? Our target doesn't have Br. Maybe the target is the precursor (before bromination) and we need to add Br. The product after bromination would have Br substituting H. The given SMILES is the precursor? It has many Cl, but no Br. So the bromination would replace a hydrogen with Br, giving product with Br. So we need template that adds Br to aromatic ring. The precursor is the given SMILES. So we need a template that when applied retrosynthetically (i.e., reverse) will give a precursor with H (i.e., remove Br). But we don't have Br in target, so maybe we need to apply forward template to precursor to get product with Br. However the task: "return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule below, reproduces the reaction". So we need a template that when applied to the given molecule (the substrate) yields product with Br. So we need to find a template that adds Br to aromatic ring. Let's search for templates where functional_groups_formed: halide, and maybe product contains Br. But search is based on target molecule (product). Our target is substrate (no Br). So maybe we need to search for templates that can be applied to this molecule to produce a brominated product. The search tool uses forward reaction criteria based on target molecule (product). So we should set molecule_smiles as the product after bromination (i.e., with Br). But we don't have that. Could generate? The substrate is Nc1c(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c1Cl (pentachloro aniline). Adding Br at one position yields Nc1c(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c1Cl with Br replacing H at some position (maybe one of the positions already Cl? Actually all positions are Cl except one with N? The ring has 6 positions: N attached, and 5 Cl substituents? The SMILES: N attached to aromatic carbon, then c(Cl) repeated 5 times, and final c1Cl. So all positions are substituted, no H left. So bromination cannot occur. Something off.

Maybe the given SMILES is the product after bromination of an aniline (with Br). But the SMILES shows Cl not Br. Could be a mistake; maybe they used Cl as placeholder for halide. The template search results show many with Cl. So maybe they want halogenation (Cl) but description says bromination. We'll just pick a template that matches halogenation (Cl) on aromatic ring. Among results, the first template (reaction_id 51493) seems to involve Cl addition to aromatic ring (Cl-[Cl]...). Mapped_rxn shows product with Cl attached to aromatic carbon. That seems appropriate.

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The template_id likely is the reaction_id? Or maybe template_id is integer identifier of template. In search results, each entry has 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash'. The template_id likely is reaction_id? The prompt says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash) as an integer". So use reaction_id.

Thus choose first entry: reaction_id 51493, mapped_rxn given.

Let's extract mapped_rxn: 'Cl[Cl:10].[O:1]=[N+:2]([O-:3])[C:4]1=[CH:5][C:6]([Cl:7])=[CH:8][C:9]([N+](=O)[O-])=[CH:11]1.O=[N+]([O-])C1=CC=CC([N+](=O)[O-])=C1>>[O:1]=[N+:2]([O-:3])[C:4]1=[CH:5][C:6]([Cl:7])=[CH:8][C:9]([Cl:10])=[CH:11]1'

But this seems to involve nitro groups etc, not our substrate. Might not be appropriate.

Second entry reaction_id 115382 mapped_rxn: '[O:1]=[N+:2]([O-:3])[C:4]1=[CH:5][CH:6]=[C:8]([OH:9])[CH:10]=[CH:12]1.[ClH:7].Cl[Cl:11].O=[N+]([O-])C1=C(O)C=CC=C1.O>>[O:1]=[N+:2]([O-:3])[C:4]1=[CH:5][C:6]([Cl:7])=[C:8]([OH:9])[C:10]([Cl:11])=[CH:12]1'

Again not simple.

Maybe we need to search specifically for aromatic halogenation templates. Let's search with functional_groups_formed: halide, and maybe functional_groups_broken: none. Already did. The results include many complex molecules. But we need a template that adds halogen to aromatic carbon (C-H -> C-Br). Could be a generic electrophilic aromatic substitution template. Let's search for templates with simple pattern: [cH:1]>>[cBr:1] maybe. Use search without molecule_smiles? Not allowed. Could search with a simple benzene SMILES "c1ccccc1". Let's try search with that to get generic template.
